items.title: Storm Charles causes floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe
items.desc: Heavy rain and strong winds have also caused disruption across British Columbia, Canada, over the last week Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain. Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November. A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours. In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations.After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy. This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera. The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia. Instead, an unspecified problem forced the company to abort recovery of the booster, which was diverted from its return path and crashed down into the Gulf of Mexico. Analysis by journalist Frédéric Castel, based in Bosa Chica, Texas, USA.

items.title: Youth Olympic Games organisers hail Senegal's capability to host major events
items.desc: Dakar 2026 is over. Two weeks of competition, thousands of young athletes and a historic first for Africa. The Youth Olympic Games brought the world to Senegal for the first Olympic sporting event ever held on the continent. From record-breaking performances to historic medals for the host nation, Dakar 2026 has been a celebration of sport, youth and cultural exchange. Our correspondent Aminatou Diallo reports from Dakar.

items.title: France and Cambodia share their love for pétanque in Phnom Penh
items.desc: Phnom Penh is hosting the 20th Francophonie Summit this Sunday and Monday. French President Emmanuel Macron is attending as part of a 3-day state visit to Cambodia. France and Cambodia's history is deep rooted and complex, but the two countries have one thing in common: a love for pétanque. Story by Caitlin Brown.

items.title: Washington divided over how to deal with fallout from the Nvidia case
items.desc: After the fall, the fallout. US government agencies are squabbling after AI leader Jensen Huang stepped down from chips giant Nvidia in disgrace. The Treasury says it wanted to blacklist a Singapore company at the heart of the scandal, but the Commerce Department didn't act. Megaspeed was run by suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang, who reportedly had an affair with Jensen Huang. Details by Peter O'Brien.

items.title: US: What exactly caused the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years?
items.desc: After a nearly five-hour ground stoppage, flights in the US have resumed. However, officials are warning that it will take days to recover from the ongoing delays related to the incident. Transport Secretary Sean Duffy explained the crisis was due to a failure in ageing telecommunications equipment. What exactly happened? Answers with FRANCE 24 international affairs editor Shirli Sitbon.

items.title: US Transport Secretary asks Congress for $30 bn to upgrade aviation infrastructure
items.desc: A failure in aging telecommunications equipment Friday forced a nationwide halt to departures from US airports. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin says officials have found no evidence so far of a cyberattack, but that they're not ruling it out. Details by Jack Pownall.

items.title: Wales claim historic victory against All Blacks for first time since 1953
items.desc: Wales claimed a historic 35-28 victory over New Zealand in Cardiff on Saturday, securing their first win over the All Blacks since 1953.

items.title: 'Poisoned chalice': French presidential hopeful Riner rebuffs Macron's backing
items.desc: French judo champion Teddy Riner on Saturday publicly distanced himself from President Emmanuel Macron, calling his endorsement a "poisoned chalice". The presidential hopeful seeks to position himself as an alternative to France's political extremes.

items.title: DR Congo, Rwanda clash over Francophonie leadership as Macron seeks compromise
items.desc: DR Congo and Rwanda clashed Saturday over the leadership of the Francophonie, as tensions between the neighbouring countries spilled into the race to head the 53-member organisation. French President Emmanuel Macron urged Rwanda to withdraw its candidate in favour of a compromise choice ahead of Monday's vote.

items.title: 'I never imagined my father was a Nazi': Born in a German
items.desc: Two trainloads of children, some of them born in Nazi-run "Lebensborn" maternity homes, were brought from Germany to Commercy in eastern France in 1946. One of those on board was Édith Pagot.

items.title: USA: All passengers survive after tanker hits docked river cruise ship in New Orleans
items.desc: A portion of the Mississippi River remains closed after a collision between an oil tanker and a riverboat forced a chaotic river rescue in Louisiana. Story by Caitlin Brown.

items.title: Inside Ethiopia's war: Rare access to a hospital treating victims of renewed fighting
items.desc:
Ethiopia's renewed conflict is taking an increasing toll on civilians, with humanitarian organisations reporting a rise in casualties. In the Amhara region, FRANCE 24’s correspondent Tom Canetti was granted rare access to a civilian hospital where surgeons are struggling to treat the influx of wounded patients. But for many caught in the fighting, reaching medical care is a challenge in itself.
 
Warning: The report contains images of surgery that may be confronting for some viewers.

items.title: Who are the 'street medics' showing up at protests around the world?
items.desc: From treating tear gas exposure to tending to injuries, street medics have become an increasingly common sight at protests all over the world. But who exactly are they and when did they start showing up at demonstrations? Story by Daniel Quinlan.

items.title: U2 releases first new studio album in a decade, 'Caranaval de Luz'
items.desc: U2 just released a new album after nine years of no new content. And fans are already rocking out to the new songs. Details on the Irish rock band’s comeback by Ophelie Jacobson.

items.title: Half a million people gather for an open-air mass by Pope Leo in Peru
items.desc: Pope Leo said it was a "joy to be back" in his second home of Chiclayo, where he made his name as a bishop. This is the latest stop on his South America tour, the very tour that saw fears of cancellation after the Pope underwent surgery for lung cancer. Story by Vedika Bahl.

items.title: Microsoft's widespread outages caused global chaos, including in the healthcasre industry
items.desc: Microsoft says it is seeing improvements in its service availability after an hours-long disruption knocked out its platforms including Outlook and Teams. The outage has affected hundreds of millions of people across the globe. The healthcare industry was among those impacted, as Ophelie Jacobson explains.

items.title: France fend off South African comeback to clinch long
items.desc: Twenty-one years after last beating the Springboks in Paris, Les Bleus held out for a 21-19 win over the world champions on Friday after a nailbiting finale. Antoine Dupont and company are now one step away from reaching the Nations Championship final in London.

items.title: US proposed Ukraine cedes Donbas in exchange for joining NATO, Zelensky says
items.desc: President Zelensky said the US had proposed ceding Ukraine's eastern city of Donbas to Russia, in exchange for Ukrainian membership of NATO, following the latest round of peace talks in Abu Dhabi this week. He reiterated that Kyiv was not willing to retreat from its territory and warned that the Kremlin's bid to change the continent's security architecture could lead to more wars.

items.title: 'Climate action is alive': Triumphant Democrats attend COP31 summit shunned by Trump
items.desc: A delegation of 18 Democratic lawmakers arrived at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey on Saturday to reaffirm the US commitment to tackling global warming following their sweeping midterm election victory.

items.title: SpaceX's Starship encounters problems during 15th test flight
items.desc: Elon Musk’s SpaceX successfully launched its Starship, the world's largest spaceship, into orbit where it should release 15 satellites for its Starlink network. A few minutes after lift off however, the rocket's booster which was meant to return to the pad splashed down in the Gulf of Mexico. Details by Daniel Quinlan.

items.title: Can Nvidia survive without tech titan Jensen Huang?
items.desc: The Financial Times says computing giant Nvidia has approached Rene Haas, CEO of British chip designer Arm, in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang. Huang resigned after his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Meanwhile some employees are clamouring for Huang's return – as his fellow tech leader Elon Musk. A sign of Huang's lingering star power, in an industry where so often the fate of each giant company depends on one man. Story by Peter O'Brien.

items.title: France's school principals say threats and violence have become unbearable
items.desc: Headteachers gathered across France this Friday, to demonstrate their frustration after nearly two months of student protests that have blockaded high schools. Many of the teachers support the students, but say they feel exhausted and isolated as the violence has surged. They are calling the government to protect them. Story by Vedika Bahl.

items.title: France protests for fifth Saturday against living costs and heavy
items.desc: Different causes are set to come together for one march in Paris this Saturday. Campaign groups, students and Yellow Vest protesters are due to join forces in the capital, bringing together demands on wages, education and civil liberties. But after weeks of demonstrations, union leaders warn that protest fatigue is setting in, while police officers are seeking better compensation for the risk of policing the protests. Story by Jack Pownall.

items.title: US nationwide flight ground stop: "Our routers got overloaded with data"
items.desc: On Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop. More than 8,200 flights, or over 31% of those scheduled in the United States, were canceled. The ground stop lasted nearly five hours and was the longest in the country since September 11, 2001. Officials blamed outdated air traffic communications equipment, and said that there was no evidence of a cyber attack. The airspace is now reopened and flights have resumed.

items.title: COP31：气候资金难满足需求，各方呼吁污染者“买单”
items.desc: 第31届联合国气候变化大会（COP31）周五聚焦气候资金问题。联合国秘书长古特雷斯警告，即使将提供给脆弱国家的气候适应资金增至三倍，也只能满足其需求的不到三成。与会者呼吁富裕国家和主要污染者承担应有责任，为受气候灾害影响的国家和社区提供更多支持。

items.title: 联合国：海湾局势持续紧张对国际和平与安全构成严重风险
items.desc: 联合国负责政治事务的助理秘书长希阿里周五在安理会通报中东局势时表示，霍尔木兹海峡和曼德海峡及其周边地区局势持续紧张，对国际和平与安全、地区稳定和全球经济构成严重风险。他呼吁各方立即停止袭击民用船舶，恢复航行自由，通过外交途径寻求和平解决方案。

items.title: 联合国环境署：空气污染不仅是环境问题，更是健康与经济危机
items.desc: 第31届联合国气候变化大会举行之际，德里及印度北部多地再次被浓重雾霾笼罩。联合国环境规划署表示，空气污染已不仅是环境问题，更是一场影响公众健康和经济发展的危机。

items.title: 世卫组织在中国设立新的全球合作中心 推进性传播感染预防与创新
items.desc: 世界卫生组织周五宣布，正式指定位于中国广州的南方医科大学全球健康研究院为新的“世卫组织性传播感染预防与创新合作中心”。此举旨在加强全球预防和控制性传播感染的合作，重点推动创新、扩大检测可及性、加强监测以及提升公共卫生能力，特别是在中低收入国家。

items.title: 刚果（金）：武装袭击阻碍埃博拉疫情防控
items.desc: 联合国应急响应人员周五警告，刚果民主共和国（刚果（金））埃博拉疫情仍在蔓延，武装团体接连袭击平民和一线医护人员，严重阻碍接触者追踪、患者救治等防疫工作。

items.title: 生命攸关：人道主义工作者呼吁迅速向加沙运送冬季物资
